frozen_for: M2 — the answer-to-feature-and-weight map for the shop
notes: This file is the single source of truth for the questionnaire and the mapping
onto the model inputs. The team tunes it here, not in code (see AGENTS.md model rules).
The model (ml_recommender.py) takes EXACTLY these customer keys and nothing else:
Any key added here that the forest was not trained on is SILENTLY IGNORED by
score_catalog_ml (it reindexes to MODEL_COLUMNS with fill_value=0). So the map
below never invents a new input; it folds answers onto the 4 trained priorities.

questions.question: What is your budget?
questions.help: Pick the closest range. We will never show you a phone above it.

questions.question: What will you use it for most?
questions.help: This decides what we look at first.

questions.question: What matters most to you?
questions.help: Just the one. We will weight it highest.

options.label: Screen
options.why: The forest has no screen input. Refresh rate is part of performance_score, so Screen folds into performance rather than being dropped. FLAG FOR M3: if screen really matters to buyers it needs its own feature.

options.label: Lowest price
options.why: The forest has NO budget_priority input — the budget weight is fixed at 0.30 and no slider can move it. So 'lowest price' is honoured by the HARD price filter instead. Honest, and it actually works.

questions.question: How much storage do you need?
questions.help: This is a hard requirement. We will not show a phone with less.

questions.question: Any brand you prefer?
questions.help: Optional. Skipping gives you the widest choice.

hard_filters.why_first: The forest regresses a score and CANNOT enforce a rule. Stock, active, budget_min and storage_min must be applied to the candidate list BEFORE the forest scores anything (AGENTS.md D34).
hard_filters.price_max_why: Hard cap with no overage tolerance. scoring.py allows 15% overage, but the shop must not show a shopper a phone above the range they picked.
hard_filters.price_min_why: Used for reporting and for the 'lowest price' cap only, NOT as a filter. A shopper who picks NGN 300k-500k should still be shown a great NGN 280k phone.
hard_filters.lowest_price_extra_cap_why: When top_priority = lowest price, cap the candidate set at 75% of budget_max, then re-sort the picks cheapest-first via questionnaire_mapper.reorder_for_lowest_price. MEASURED: the cap ALONE was not enough — the forest returned a NGN 556,000 phone as pick #1 while a NGN 98,100 Redmi 13C was available. The cap filters; the re-sort orders.

priority_map.how: The questionnaire asks for ONE top priority. The model wants FOUR low/medium/high sliders. Rule: the chosen one becomes 'high', the rest stay 'medium' (not 'low', so we do not punish the other categories).
priority_map.storage: from the storage question only: light=low, medium=medium, heavy=high
priority_map.storage_why: Storage has its own question, so it gets a real measured level instead of a guess, and top_priority never overrides it.
priority_map.lowest_price_fallback: When top_priority==lowest_price all four become 'low', so no single spec category dominates and the price filter does the real work.

reasons.ratings_from: scoring.py component scores (camera_score, battery_score, performance_score, storage_score)
reasons.why: Reason lines are still built by scoring.py, NOT by the forest. Ranking and reasons stay decoupled (see the ml_recommender.py header).
